title: Your agent architecture has a half-life of 6 months — Dan Farrelly, CTO, Inngest
talk_summary: Dan Farrelly argues agent architectures decay fast because teams couple three layers with different half-lives: execution (durable, years), context (models/prompts/tools, weeks-months), and compute (sandboxes, ephemeral). He says invest in a decoupled execution layer that provides resumability, flexible invocation primitives, and full-session observability, and treat sandboxes as stateless hands, not state stores.

takeaways.technique: Externalize run state from the worker/sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep durable run state outside the process and sandbox so a failed step can be retried and resumed rather than restarting the whole run; sandboxes are treated as ephemeral and stateless.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a 3-hour run cannot hold state in memory or in disk. The state must live outside of the work.

takeaways.technique: Sandbox as disposable hands, not state store
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the sandbox as ephemeral compute that the execution layer gives context and sequence to; do not use snapshots or sandbox disk for durability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a sandbox is ephemeral and stateless by design. So, using it for durability, snapshots, or something in state, I think is an anti-pattern.

takeaways.what_they_do: Provide one execution layer supporting crons, event triggers, APIs, human-in-the-loop, subagents, sync/async/delayed invocation, so harness logic doesn't absorb queues, polling, backoff, scheduling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your harness logic starts absorbing other concepts like queues, workers, polling, backoff, scheduling.

takeaways.technique: Outcome-based scoring attached to execution traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument the execution layer to defer scoring after a run using the full trace plus later events (did a PR open? was research saved?) instead of thumbs up/down.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of a thumbs up, thumbs down, it's like did we open the PR, right?

takeaways.technique: Self-improving review loop over execution history
takeaways.what_they_do: A scheduled reviewer function pulls logs of what agents executed and chose, evaluates performance, and proposes prompt/metric changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it needs to be able to pull the logs of the system and understand, all right, what was executed?

takeaways.technique: Full-session trace across trigger to completion
takeaways.what_they_do: Observability must span LLM calls, tool calls, DB errors, permissions, triggers, and performance for the whole session, not just model calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can't see the entirety of a trace from the trigger through the whole stack, it's really hard to debug it
